clue.text: Bad animal in Orwell's farm

parts.note: in Animal Farm the sheep bleat 'Four legs good, two legs bad', so the bad animal is the one that walks on two legs

explanation.walkthrough: In George Orwell's novel Animal Farm the animals chant 'Four legs good, two legs bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-legged creature, such as a human, is exactly what the farm animals' slogan condemns.

clue.text: Hoarding banknote to get food

parts.note: bill is the American word for a banknote
board means meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiling money to pay for meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoarding' looks like stockpiling but is the British word for a large advertising board; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a hoarding is a large outdoor advertising board.

clue.text: Waste on Corporation plantation

parts.note: to pine is to waste away
corporation is an old humorous word for a large belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Waste is dumped on land owned by a corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is jocular British slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinetum is a planting of pine trees grown for study or display.

clue.text: Fly, bird

definitions.meaning: a ... is a mayfly, or an angler's artificial fly imitating one

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a mayfly used in fishing and a male duck.

clue.text: Aquiline-looking pirate sniffed

parts.note: Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan
to nose is to sniff about

explanation.surface: A pirate with a beaky profile sniffs the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquiline face has a curved, beak-like nose like an eagle's.

clue.text: Judge has to pronounce this evidence is inadmissible

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it
to say is to pronounce

explanation.surface: A judge rules that some evidence cannot be allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: rumour heard from others is not admissible evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand report of what others said is generally barred as evidence in court.

clue.text: Nonconformist not even dancing

parts.note: an odd number is not even
a ball is a social event for dancing

explanation.surface: A chapel-goer who refuses even to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonconformist' suggests a Protestant dissenter but means an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person who does not follow convention is a nonconformist.

clue.text: One who counts, to put it another way, is true Roman

indicators.note: putting the words another way rearranges the letters of true Roman

explanation.surface: Another way of saying a genuine Roman can count.
explanation.definitionFit: A numerator is a person who numbers or counts things.

clue.text: Substitute's prolonged resistance when batting

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, the link to the wordplay

parts.note: a stand is a prolonged resistance, as a last stand
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A substitute holds out at the crease when batting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is 'in' while batting, and a long partnership is a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is someone who substitutes for another.

clue.text: Search for water for duck

definitions.meaning: to look for underground water with a divining rod
to duck is to plunge into water, a variant spelling of douse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both divining for water and dunking someone.

clue.text: Provide a bunch of bananas for support

parts.note: to lend is to give or provide
a hand is the trade term for a cluster of bananas

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a bunch of bananas to keep a friend going.
explanation.definitionFit: To help or assist someone is idiomatically to give them a helping hand.

clue.text: Macavity in an old wardrobe starts to wail thus?

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters, one taken from each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A cat shut in an old wardrobe begins to howl.
explanation.walkthrough: Macavity is the mystery cat of T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, so the cry fits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's plaintive cry is the sound written as its mewing call.

clue.text: Meeting place in London for North and South to make pounds each at card game

definitions.text: Meeting place in London for North and South

parts.note: to batter is to pound repeatedly
bridge is the card game in which North and South are partners

explanation.surface: North and South meet at a bridge table in London and win a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South are the partners at bridge, but the definition means the Thames crossing joining the north and south banks of London; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Thames crossing links Chelsea on the north bank with Battersea on the south.

clue.text: Array of weapons belonging to us in the Forces

indicators.note: in places the words for belonging to us within the word for the Forces

parts.note: the army is one of the armed forces
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Our weapons are held by the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: A store of arms kept ready for use is an arsenal.

clue.text: Understood — like the end of Edwin Drood, for example

definitions.meaning: understood means tacit, agreed without being set down

definitions.text: like the end of Edwin Drood, for example
definitions.meaning: Dickens died before finishing The Mystery of Edwin Drood, so its ending was never set down

explanation.definitionFit: Tacit rules and a book's never-completed ending are both never put on paper.

clue.text: Hidden capacity of any Celt to be devious

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding, twisted path, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Any Celt has a hidden talent for being cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ANY and CELT are rearranged; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latency is a potential that exists but is not yet shown or active, a dormant ability.

clue.text: Windswept traveller

parts.note: a voyager driven along by the wind, that is, sailing a pleasure boat

explanation.definitionFit: A sailor of a pleasure boat is literally swept along by the wind.

clue.text: Does not claim to plant in rows

indicators.note: in tells us one word is put inside the other, the word for plant within the word for rows

parts.note: a row is a noisy din
to sow is to plant seed

explanation.surface: A gardener refuses to plant in neat lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like garden lines but means noisy quarrels, DINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to acknowledge something is to deny it is yours.

clue.text: Drive up and down to find heavenly colour

parts.note: to sky a ball is to drive it high into the air
down means sad or blue

explanation.surface: A driver goes up and down hills looking for a celestial shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale blue of a clear sky is the heavenly shade.

clue.text: Fruit in South Africa giving rise to a new wine

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so a and the word for new wine are turned round

parts.note: must is unfermented new grape juice

explanation.surface: A fruit grown in South Africa is turned into a new wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' turns A MUST into TSUMA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: It may come from sewer rat I caught wandering

indicators.note: the run of letters can come out of the words sewer rat I caught, spanning them

explanation.surface: A rat caught in the sewer is unpredictable in its movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic strays without a fixed course, roving irregularly.

clue.text: Put up before the court, man's made to look small

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
ct is the abbreviation for court
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man brought before the court is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to look small' tells us court and man are cut down to short forms, CT and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built or raised up has been erected.

clue.text: America's whirlwind crook

definitions.meaning: in the US a ... is a tornado

explanation.definitionFit: The word is US slang for a tornado and British slang for a cheat.

clue.text: One who's not well treated by this manipulative person?

definitions.text: One who's not well treated by this manipulative person?

parts.words: One who's not well treated by this manipulative person?
parts.note: the patient is someone unwell, and the manipulative person is a therapist who manipulates muscles and joints, not a schemer

explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who treats injury by massage and manipulation of the body.

clue.text: Head of police called to crash

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from police

parts.note: rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: A police chief phones in to report a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is a minor collision, especially in a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Receive grant

definitions.meaning: to let in or receive a visitor
to concede or grant a point

explanation.definitionFit: Letting someone in and conceding a point are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Apportion a reverse charge

indicators.note: reverse tells us the word for charge is turned round

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Someone sharing out the cost of a reverse-charge phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse charge' looks like a collect call, but 'reverse' turns TOLL into LLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions.

clue.text: Mutual mistake about man's final offer

annotationWithheld.why: Mutual mistake about man's final offer (9): an anagram of MUTUAL leaves I, T, M to come from 'man's', which no reading supplies
annotationWithheld.clue: Mutual mistake about man's final offer

clue.text: Come down on grass strip in island

indicators.note: on means the word for come down is placed after the grass strip, in this across clue

parts.note: a green is a strip of grass, as on a golf course or village
to land is to come down from the air

explanation.surface: A plane lands on a grass airstrip on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's largest island, an autonomous territory of Denmark.

clue.text: I go round city with shroud

indicators.note: round means the word for go is placed around the letter I

parts.note: a turn is a go in a game
I is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tour of a city famous for a shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turin Shroud is a linen cloth said to bear the image of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city whose cathedral keeps the famous holy relic cloth.
